facts.text: Esopus derives its name from the Lenape word that translates to 'Wellspring of Creation'.
Christoffel 'Kit' Davits, a trapper, was the first known European to settle in Esopus, trading with the local Esopus people.
In 1777 a colonial prison was built in Esopus to house overflow from a prison ship, only for the British to burn the settlement that same year.
Esopus was briefly considered as a United Nations headquarters site in 1946 before the plan moved to Manhattan.
Three properties in Esopus—Oliver Hazard Payne Estate, Poppletown Farmhouse, and the Reformed Protestant Dutch Church of Klyne Esopus—are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
